response.text:
Using the standard Rayleigh nitrogen data

\[
\begin{aligned}
\text{Chemical: }&2.30143,2.29890,2.29816,2.30182,2.29869,2.29940,2.29849,2.29889,\\
\text{Atmospheric: }&2.31017,2.30986,2.31010,2.31001,2.31024,2.31010,2.31028,2.31001,
\end{aligned}
\]

let \(\mu_C\) be the mean mass for nitrogen from chemical compounds and \(\mu_A\) the mean mass for atmospheric nitrogen. I use a two-sample Welch \(t\)-procedure, since the sample variances are quite different.

## (1) Test for difference in means

We test

\[
H_0:\mu_A-\mu_C=0
\qquad\text{vs.}\qquad
H_1:\mu_A-\mu_C\neq 0.
\]

The sample summaries are

\[
\bar x_C=2.2994725,\qquad s_C=0.0013792,\qquad n_C=8,
\]

\[
\bar x_A=2.3100963,\qquad s_A=0.0001366,\qquad n_A=8.
\]

Thus

\[
\bar x_A-\bar x_C=0.0106238.
\]

The Welch standard error is

\[
SE=\sqrt{\frac{s_A^2}{n_A}+\frac{s_C^2}{n_C}}
   =\sqrt{\frac{(0.0001366)^2}{8}+\frac{(0.0013792)^2}{8}}
   \approx 0.0004900.
\]

The test statistic is

\[
t=\frac{0.0106238}{0.0004900}\approx 21.68.
\]

The Welch–Satterthwaite degrees of freedom are approximately

\[
\nu \approx 7.14.
\]

Therefore the two-sided \(p\)-value is

\[
p=2P\left(T_{7.14}\ge 21.68\right)\approx 9\times 10^{-8}.
\]

So the \(p\)-value is extremely small. There is overwhelming evidence that the mean mass of nitrogen per flask differs between the two sources. In particular, atmospheric nitrogen appears heavier on average.

A distribution-free permutation/rank test would also reject strongly; since all atmospheric observations exceed all chemical observations, the exact two-sided rank-based \(p\)-value for the \(8\)-by-\(8\) data is

\[
\frac{2}{\binom{16}{8}}\approx 1.55\times 10^{-4}.
\]

That is larger than the Welch \(t\)-test \(p\)-value but still highly significant.

## (2) 95% confidence interval for the mean difference

A 95% Welch confidence interval for \(\mu_A-\mu_C\) is

\[
(\bar x_A-\bar x_C)\pm t_{0.975,\nu}SE.
\]

With \(\nu\approx 7.14\),

\[
t_{0.975,7.14}\approx 2.36.
\]

Hence

\[
0.0106238\pm 2.36(0.0004900)
=
0.0106238\pm 0.001155.
\]

Therefore,

\[
\boxed{(0.00947,\;0.01178)}
\]

is a 95% confidence interval for

\[
\mu_A-\mu_C.
\]

Equivalently, for \(\mu_C-\mu_A\), the interval is

\[
\boxed{(-0.01178,\;-0.00947)}.
\]

Thus atmospheric nitrogen is estimated to have mean mass about \(0.0106\) grams per flask larger than nitrogen from chemical compounds.
